review_candidates.title: Systems Administrator
review_candidates.description: The Role We're seeking a Systems Administrator to architect, deploy, secure, and maintain the core systems powering our organization — spanning both corporate IT and the operational technology (OT) behind our deployed microgrids. This dual role blends hands-on engineering with day-to-day administration, with heavy emphasis on access/permissions management, security hardening and compliance (NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2), network administration, remote connectivity, and monitoring across IT and field OT assets. Strong networking fundamentals are required; hands-on OT/ICS experience in energy, utilities, or renewables is strongly preferred. This hybrid role will report to our Sr Manager, IT and be based in our HQ in Ridgewood, NJ. Key responsibilities will include: Systems Engineering: Design, deploy, and maintain server, storage, and virtualized infrastructure (cloud and on-prem), including Windows Server, Linux, Active Directory/Azure AD, and automation/IaC practices Administration: Own identity and access management end-to-end (onboarding/offboarding, role-based permissions, MFA, privileged access, backups, audit logging); apply patches/updates and maintain system health and availability Security & Compliance: Serve as primary owner of access governance and least-privilege design; administer EDR, SIEM, MDM, and vulnerability management tools; extend controls into OT (segmentation, secure remote access); support SOC 2/ISO 27001 audit readiness and incident response Troubleshooting & Support: Provide Tier 1–3 support across Windows, macOS, Linux, virtualization, and cloud; engage vendors as needed Cloud Administration: Manage Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Azure (VMs, storage, identity, conditional access); implement cloud backup/DR Network & Connectivity: Design and maintain switching, routing, VLANs, firewalls, and VPNs; configure cellular modems/gateways for microgrid site connectivity (carrier/APN/SIM provisioning, NAT, failover); build secure IT/OT remote access paths OT & Field Systems: Support microgrid controllers, PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, inverters, and meters; troubleshoot protocol-level issues (Modbus, DNP3, MQTT, SNMP, BACnet); partner with Scale’s control team for on-site commissioning and OT patch/firmware management Monitoring & Observability: Build and tune monitoring/alerting across IT and OT (health, connectivity, data flow, backups, security events); create dashboards and reduce MTTD/MTTR Documentation: Maintain system/network diagrams, SOPs, configuration baselines, and runbooks; generate performance and capacity reports The Ideal Candidate Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience); 5+ years as a Systems Engineer/Administrator with direct network administration responsibility OT/ICS/SCADA experience in energy, utilities, renewables, or industrial/building systems strongly preferred Demonstrated experience with NIST, ISO 27001, and/or SOC 2 frameworks Certifications preferred: Network+/Security+, CCNA, Azure Administrator, MCSA/MCSE, RHCSA, GICSP, or similar Technical Proficiency: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu/CentOS), Active Directory, Azure AD, Group Policy, M365; VMware/Hyper-V Strong networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, subnetting, routing, VLANs, DNS/DHCP, NAT, firewalls, VPNs Hands-on experience with cellular modems/industrial gateways (Cradlepoint, Sierra Wireless, Digi, Teltonika, Peplink) and carrier/SIM management Monitoring/alerting tools (PRTG, SolarWinds, Datadog, Zabbix, Grafana); backup/DR platforms (Veeam, Datto) Familiarity with industrial protocols and IT/OT segmentation; Zero Trust and NIST 800-82/IEC 62443 knowledge a plus Strong analytical and communication skills; highly organized and detail-oriented; collaborative, customer-focused mindset Willingness to travel to office, project, and client sites, including field visits to operating microgrid sites. Approximate travel 25% Ability to participate in an on-call rotation and evening/nighttime system migration tasks when required This is a great opportunity to have a long-term impact on a fast-paced, private equity-backed growth business. Some of the core virtues embraced by Scales’ employees include: Do the Right Thing Act Like an Owner Hustle Demand Results Go Together Evolve or Disappear We offer a competitive compensation package and a comprehensive benefits program including medical benefits, paid vacation and holidays, and 401K matching. About Scale Microgrids Scale is redefining resilience, with advanced microgrids that go beyond traditional backup power solutions to give businesses the power to adapt and thrive amid all of today’s growing energy challenges. As a vertically-integrated provider of turnkey advanced microgrid systems, Scale combines project design, engineering, and execution expertise with microgrid-as-a-service financing to offer our customers systems that are optimized to deliver maximum value from day one while ensuring ultra-reliable operations and fast time-to-power. Scale is backed by EQT, a firm with :$250B in assets, bringing a depth of experience, resources, and capital that will enable Scale to continue pursuing our vision of powering the world with distributed energy. The investment enables Scale to own and operate billions of dollars in distributed generation assets. To learn more about Scale Microgrids, please visit https://www.scalemicrogrids.com. About EQT EQT is a leading purpose-driven global investment organization with EUR 246 billion in total assets under management, divided into two business segments: Private Capital and Real Assets. EQT owns portfolio companies and assets in Europe, Asia Pacific, and the Americas and supports them in achieving sustainable growth, operational excellence, and market leadership. To learn more about EQT, please visit https://eqtgroup.com. Scale strives to attract and retain a workforce that reflects the composition of our customer base and communities. Ideal candidates will have a broad set of technical skills and must be able to work both independently and within a team environment. As a member of our team, you will play a key role in ensuring that systems with a direct impact on our country's warfighting and peacekeeping capabilities perform at optimal levels. The Systems and Network Administrator provides support to U.S. Navy programs by administering and maintaining mixed Windows and Linux server environments and the supporting local network infrastructure used by mission-critical development, test, and operational systems. This is a hands-on infrastructure role in a laboratory environment rather than a full-scale Network Operations Center. The position is responsible for server and virtualization administration, basic managed-switch and endpoint configuration, network documentation, connectivity troubleshooting, and system security in compliance with DoD cybersecurity policies and Navy operational requirements. This position is located at our customer site at Joint Base MDL. You will work our customer's Compressed Work Schedule, which consists of four 9-hour days (Monday-Thursday) and one 8-hour day (Friday) during the first week of the cycle, followed by four 9-hour days (Monday-Thursday) and Friday off during the second week. This results in a three-day weekend every other week! RESPONSIBILITIES Install, configure, secure, and maintain Windows Server and Linux operating systems in development, integration, test, and production environments. Administer user accounts, permissions, directory services, and Group Policy in accordance with approved access-control and cybersecurity requirements. Monitor system health and resource utilization; perform performance tuning and troubleshoot hardware, operating system, application-hosting, and availability issues. Manage server and network-device patching, updates, vulnerability remediation, configuration backups, and lifecycle maintenance. Administer and support virtualized environments such as VMware, Hyper-V, or comparable platforms. Install and configure managed network switches, including access ports, VLAN assignments, port security, firmware, and saved configurations, within approved network designs. Configure servers, workstations, test equipment, and other endpoints for network connectivity, including network interfaces, IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, and approved security settings. Troubleshoot physical and logical connectivity issues involving cabling, switch ports, VLANs, addressing, name resolution, and routing; document findings and coordinate escalation when required. Support physical network infrastructure, including racks, cabling, labeling, and connection management for laboratory and test environments. Maintain system and network documentation, architecture diagrams, IP address plans, port maps, asset records, and configuration baselines. Support the integration of systems and endpoints into secure Navy networks and enclaves in coordination with network, cybersecurity, and infrastructure stakeholders. Collaborate with developers, cybersecurity personnel, system administrators, and engineers to support application hosting, laboratory operations, accreditation activities, and incident resolution. Assist with infrastructure support for DevSecOps pipelines and containerized environments, and provide technical recommendations for reliability, security, modernization, and performance improvements. QUALIFICATIONS: A BS/BA degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field is preferred. Equivalent work experience is acceptable in lieu of a degree.
